title: Orchestration hub weekly huddle notes (sept 7 2027)
content:
Orchestration hub weekly huddle — 2027-09-07
Owners: Aisha Patel (notes), Miguel Santos (routing), Jordan Li (auth), Priya Desai (quotas)

Attendees:
- Aisha, Miguel, Jordan, Priya, Samir, Devinder (SRE), Lina (solutions eng) — casual drop-ins from product and console team for the second half.

Quick summary / purpose:
- Short sync to align on execution for the next 10 days for the orchestration surface: routing policy rollouts, auth resilience work, and quota behaviour experiments. Goal: unblock canary for tiered routing and lock down mitigation steps for quota burn spikes.

Highlights / metrics since last huddle:
- Routing fallback rate (percent of requests that hit fallback routing in last 24h): 1.8% (target <0.5%). Spike correlates with two small bursts on us-east-1 on 2027-09-06 03:20–03:40 UTC.
- Auth token validation latency p99 rose to 245ms (baseline 120ms) during the same window.
- Global soft-quota throttle events triggered ~1900 requests over threshold; of those 68% were retryable and got delayed; observed ~0.3% error leakage into client bucket.
- No customer-facing outages; one internal dashboard alert chain and automatic rollback prevented wider impact.

Incidents & immediate follow-ups:
1) 03:20–03:40 burst (us-east-1) correlated with a pod churn in vm-pool-8: kube eviction (PLT-ERR-582). Action: Samir to add eviction guard for routing-controller by 2027-09-10 (see action item A1).
2) Auth validation latency bump traced to a cache stampede on auth-cache (PR 4021). Jordan to merge hotfix backport and run 24h shadow tests (A2).
3) Quota burn: onboarding job from a customer misconfigured client-side batching and created sustained burst of small requests. Priya to follow up with CS and propose tenant isolation tweak + throttle policy change (A3).

Decisions made:
- Short-term: enable routing fallback debounce (delay window 30s) for canary traffic only — reduces oscillation between tiers. Miguel to flip flag in canary by 2027-09-09.
- Medium-term: add a circuit-breaker layer in the auth proxy that uses moving-window token error counts to avoid cascading latency increases. Jordan and Miguel will prototype with canary traffic.
- Quotas: approve experiment to test token-bucket smoothing on reserved pools for 48 hours. Priya to run experiment on dedicated pool dpool-3.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- A1: Add eviction guard & graceful drain to routing-controller (Samir) — due 2027-09-10 — blocker for stable fallback enforcement.
- A2: Backport auth-cache hotfix + run shadow validation across regions (Jordan) — due 2027-09-08 — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4021.
- A3: CS follow-up + tenant isolation plan for noisy onboarding job (Priya) — due 2027-09-09 — link to case: CS-7791.
- A4: Debounce flag for canary routing (Miguel) — due 2027-09-09 — config change tracked in PLT-2121.
- A5: Quota smoothing experiment on dpool-3 (Priya + Lina) — start 2027-09-08, evaluate 2027-09-10.
- A6: Build synthetic test to reproduce routing-fallback oscillation in staging (Aisha + Devinder) — due 2027-09-12.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should fallback routing include model-quality-aware routing (i.e., prefer higher-quality variant even at higher cost) or keep it strictly latency/capacity-driven? Product wants a toggle; engineering prefers initial capacity-first approach. Tentative: capacity-first; add quality flag for next sprint.
- How aggressive should tenant isolation be for noisy onboarding flows? Isolate at tenant-level or at API-key level? Priya to propose gradation options.
- Need better visibility into cross-region token-cache state; propose adding a small tracing span at token validation path to surface cache-hit/miss ratios.

Notes from brainstorm (10m):
- Idea: introduce a lightweight predictive dampener for routing decisions that uses simple EWMA of recent reject rates to avoid flapping. Prototype idea: keep a 60s EWMA with 0.2 smoothing factor; only allow tier up/down one step per 60s. Miguel to add pseudocode to PLT-2121.
- Idea: auth proxy can emit a low-cardinality "token-hot" tag when backoff engages — will help tie latency spikes to token storms. Jordan to add metric.

Meeting artifacts / links:
- Linear tickets: PLT-2121 (routing fallbacks), AUTH-987 (auth-cache backport), QUOTA-334 (smoothing experiment).
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4021 (auth fix), https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4032 (routing debounce prototype).
- Slack thread: #platform-orchestration: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CPLATFORM/p17542348901234

Follow-ups for next huddle (2027-09-14):
- Report on canary debounce flag metrics (fallback rate target <0.5%).
- Results of quota smoothing experiment (latency, error leakage, customer impact).
- Staging reproduction of routing flap and proposed guard changes.

Quick retro / tone:
- Good cross-team responsiveness — CS flagged noisy onboarding quickly which prevented customer errors.
- Need to reduce blast radius of misconfigured onboarding jobs — agreed this should be an immediate product+engineering policy.

Appendix: quick timeline/logs (raw)
- 2027-09-06 03:20 UTC: Alert — Routing fallback spike (1.8%).
- 2027-09-06 03:23 UTC: Auth p99 245ms alert.
- 2027-09-06 03:25 UTC: Kube eviction in vm-pool-8 (PLT-ERR-582).
- 2027-09-06 03:28 UTC: Automatic canary rollback triggered for route-decision service; rollback succeeded at 03:31.
- 2027-09-06 04:10 UTC: CS surfaces misconfigured onboarding job (tenant T-448).

If anything missing, add to the doc and ping Aisha.

-- end of notes
